title: Quantized kernel conformance: harness, vectors, and tolerances
content:
Purpose:
- Define a lightweight, reproducible conformance harness for quantized execution paths (INT8 / FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ) focused on kernel correctness, numerical drift budgets, and interaction with KV cache and streaming paths.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: per-layer and end-to-end conformance tests that run as part of the serving-runtime CI and as a local validation harness for kernel authors. Does NOT replace extensive offline model-quality evals, but provides early detection of regressions introduced by kernel changes, scheduler heuristics, or KV handling.
- Goals:
  - Provide deterministic input vectors and reference float32 outputs for a representative set of layer types (attention, MLP, rotary/embed-ops, layernorm pre/post).
  - Define clear numeric tolerances per operation and a small set of end-to-end acceptance criteria (logprob delta, output token divergence metrics).
  - Include KV-cache interaction scenarios (prefix reuse, partial KV updates, cross-batch kv reuse) to catch cache-coherence/shape problems.
  - Make harness fast enough to run in pre-merge CI for kernel PRs (target < 5m per PR on a small CPU/GPU runner using reduced-size models) and thorough enough for nightly full-run.

Test vector design (format + generation):
- Vector format: flattened JSONL where each record contains: id, model-arch-tag, op-sequence, input-shapes, raw-input-bytes (base64), reference-output-bytes (base64), rng-seed, notes. Keep each vector < 1MB for quick transfer.
- Generation strategy:
  - Use a float32 reference runtime (control) to produce golden outputs and metadata. Golden runs record intermediate activations for targeted ops to allow fine-grained root-cause analysis.
  - Generate many small vectors (mini-batches and single-token cases) to stress edge shapes: sequence len=1, seq=8, seq=64, kv-split across shards, fused attention with and without rotary.
  - Include adversarial inputs: near-zero activations, large-magnitude activations, alternating sign patterns, and sparse tokens to exercise quantization edgecases.
  - Repro seed is mandatory. Vector creation tooling must be deterministic given seed + arch tag.

Per-op acceptance metrics and tolerances (starter proposal):
- Basic metrics:
  - L2-rel: relative L2 norm between reference and test op output.
  - Linf-abs: maximum absolute element-wise difference.
  - Cosine sim: for embedding-like outputs or projection vectors.
  - Quantized-bitwise-check: for ops that retain integer-like semantics.
- Proposed tolerances (configurable per model family):
  - Matmul (GEMM) after quantization (INT8/AWQ/GPTQ): L2-rel <= 6e-3, Linf-abs <= 1e-2 for scaled outputs when inputs are normalized.
  - FP8 kernels: L2-rel <= 2e-3, Linf-abs <= 5e-3 (expect tighter for FP8 on small ranges).
  - LayerNorm (FP32 reference vs quantized path): Linf-abs <= 1e-4 on normalized outputs; but for quant->dequant variants allow Linf-abs <= 1e-3.
  - Rotary/position ops: cosine sim >= 0.999 for projection slices.
  - KV concat / slice operations: exact-shape and exact-order required; numerical tolerances apply to values, but shape/ordering mismatches must be flagged as hard failures.
- End-to-end acceptance:
  - On a reduced-length generation (seeded), compute top-1 token sequence and cumulative logprob under the float32 reference. Accept if: token-sequence matches OR cumulative logprob delta <= 0.15 nats per token on average and top-5 overlap >= 0.9.
  - If sequence mismatch occurs, root-cause report must include the first layer/op where per-op metrics cross thresholds.

KV cache and streaming scenarios to include:
- Cold start single-shot generation (no KV).
- Prefix + continuation: full prefix of seq=64 cached, then a 16-token continuation; check that KV reuse yields identical outputs versus fresh-run.
- Partial-KV refresh: simulate a hot-swapped KV shard (one kv partition replaced) to ensure graceful fallbacks and detect indexing bugs.
- Interleaved streaming: simulate interleaving of two streams which share weights but not KV; ensure no cross-talk in statically allocated buffers.
- KV eviction / truncate event tests: ensure buffer compaction and offset arithmetic produce correct resulting values.

Harness architecture and runner behavior:
- Components:
  - vector-store: small L1 store of golden vectors (JSONL).
  - runner: localized binary that can load a target kernel (via library path) and execute the op-sequence against the vector with configurable precision mode (force INT8, FP8, hybrid).
  - comparator: computes per-op metrics and aggregates into the final pass/fail.
  - reporter: emits compact JSON test reports for CI and a verbose HTML diagnostic page for devs when failures occur.
- Local run command example (prototype):
  - ./quant-harness run --vector=vec001.jsonl --kernel=libawq.so --mode=int8 --emit=report.json --seed=42
- CI integration:
  - Quick-smoke job: select 40 targeted vectors across attention/MLP/KV and run against the PR-proposed kernel; required to pass within soft tolerances.
  - Nightly full-run: run the entire vector set and produce per-commit baseline metrics stored in an artifact bucket.
  - Flaky detection: any vector that flips status more than 3 times in 7 days is marked flaky and moved to an isolation suite for manual triage.

Regression detection and baselining:
- Baseline storage: store minimal summary (per-op L2-rel, Linf, cosine, end-to-end logprob delta) per commit. Use time-series to detect step changes.
- Alerting rules:
  - Blocker: any shape/ordering mismatch or hard failure in KV path; fails PR gating.
  - Major: end-to-end token divergence with logprob delta > 0.25 nats/token or sustained >3x increase in L2-rel for core GEMM ops across model family; raise incident.
  - Minor: single-op metric bump within tolerance but outside historical mean + 4*stddev; warn and annotate PR.

Handling model variants and kernel selection heuristics:
- Tag vectors with model-families: small-lm, med-lm, long-lm and with op-level flags (fused-attn, split-kv, mm-sparsity). Use tags to pick representative vectors for each kernel target.
- When scheduler selects a fallback kernel (e.g., int8->fp32 for certain layers), harness must run both the primary and fallback paths and compare to reference; differences must be annotated with the scheduler decision metadata.

Determinism, rounding, and nondeterministic sources:
- Force RNG seeds in all reference/golden runs and include seed in vector metadata.
- Lock global thread count and CUDA deterministic flags in CI runs. Document known nondeterministic ops (atomic adds in sparse accumulators) and mark them as soft-exception candidates with bespoke tolerances.

Developer UX and triage outputs:
- Failure payload should include: failing vector id, first failing op index, per-op metric table (L2, Linf, cosine), small hexdump of input slice and output slice (base64), kernel version + compile flags, and stack trace if crash.
- HTML diagnostic: heatmap per-layer of relative error, and a side-by-side waveform for attention scores to visualize drift.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Finalize numeric tolerance scaling by typical activation scale per family (small/med/long). Current numbers are conservative starter points.
- Decide on maximum allowed nightly cumulative regressions (SLO for maintainers).
- Add automated kernel bisecting flow: given a change that causes regression, automate binary search over commits/builds to isolate offending change.
- Expand vector set to include quantized QKV patterns observed in customer telemetry (Ethan to share telemetry subset).

Notes / quick wins:
- Start with a minimal runner that validates GEMM + KV concat + LayerNorm for a canonical 2-layer block. Cheap to run, fast feedback.
- Use existing small-model checkpoints (open-family distilled) as a source of realistic activation ranges to seed vectors.

References and links:
- See linked artifacts (JIRA:SRV-4123) for tracking ticket and initial PR (serving-runtime/pull/1782).
- Related: nightly numerics dashboard (confluence.redwood/serving/runtime/quant-tests).
